The Resvent iBreeze offers a longer ramp time than the DreamStation CPAP. The iBreeze CPAP System has a Ramp Time feature with a maximum range of 60 minutes (range_max: 60, with settings of "Off, 5-45 minutes in 5-minute increments, or Auto"). The ResMed AirStart 10 is quieter than the ResMed AirSense 11. The AirStart 10 CPAP has a sound pressure level of 26.6 dBA (AirStart 10 CPAP), while the AirSense 11 has a sound pressure level of 27 dBA (AirSense 11). This means the AirStart 10 is slightly quieter by 0.4 dBA.

On the DreamStation, SmartRamp mode allows users to fall asleep to lower pressures than standard ramp mode (SmartRamp entity). While the standard Ramp feature reduces pressure and then gradually increases it to the prescription setting over a set duration (Ramp entity), SmartRamp specifically focuses on providing lower pressures during the sleep onset period. The DreamStation CPAP Pro offers Smart Ramp with a 0-45 minute duration in 5-minute increments (Smart Ramp entity, DreamStation CPAP Pro entity), compared to the standard ramp which has a fixed gradual pressure increase pattern.

The ResMed AirSense 10 AutoSet for Her is the ResMed device that has a therapy algorithm designed specifically for women. It is described as an "auto-adjusting device with algorithm designed for female-specific characteristics of sleep apnea" (ResMed AirSense 10 AutoSet for Her). The device supports the "AutoSet for Her" mode (ResMed AirSense 10 AutoSet for Her), which uses the "AutoSet for Her algorithm" - the first dedicated algorithm designed to treat obstructive sleep apnea in female patients, addressing higher instances of flow limitation in women (AutoSet for Her algorithm).

The EZ-Start feature on the DreamStation CPAP Pro provides automatic, personalized adjustments to CPAP pressure designed to help patients gradually acclimate to their prescribed level of therapy. This feature enhances patient acclimation by providing personalized adjustments that allow users to become comfortable with their therapy over time.

On the Seattle-PAP bubble CPAP system, the 135-degree angle in the submersed tubing creates pressure oscillations (Seattle-PAP). These pressure oscillations provide a therapeutic effect similar to high frequency ventilation (Pressure Oscillations, Bubble CPAP Therapy). The clinical benefit of these oscillations is that they improve gas exchange and reduce respiratory muscle work in infants (Bubble CPAP Therapy). Additionally, the vibrations from the bubbling help contribute to gas exchange and reduce the infant's work of breathing (Bubble CPAP).

The ResMed AutoRamp feature relies on sleep onset detection to know when to ramp up to the prescribed pressure. According to the knowledge graph, AutoRamp is described as a "Feature with sleep onset detection that starts with low pressure and ramps up to prescribed pressure once patient falls asleep" (AutoRamp). More specifically, the "AutoRamp with sleep onset detection" feature "begins by delivering a low start pressure to help fall asleep with ease, then responds by comfortably ramping up to prescribed pressure the moment it detects sleep onset" (AutoRamp with sleep onset detection). This feature is available on ResMed devices including the AirSense 10 AutoSet and AirSense 10 AutoSet for Her.

On the ResMed AirSense 11, the EPR (Expiratory Pressure Relief) feature makes it easier to breathe out during therapy by lowering the pressure delivered when exhaling. This comfort feature gently reduces the air pressure during exhalation, making it more comfortable to breathe out against the positive airway pressure. The EPR feature has three levels of pressure reduction: Level 1 reduces pressure by 1.0 cmH2O, Level 2 reduces pressure by 2.0 cmH2O, and Level 3 reduces pressure by 3.0 cmH2O. The minimum pressure at which EPR operates is 4.0 cmH2O. EPR enhances CPAP therapy by improving comfort during the breathing cycle.
